# MastiDB

> MastiDB is a minimal, on-disk columnar OLAP database engine written in Python. It implements the core ideas that make analytical engines fast, at a size you can read in an afternoon. It is an experimental learning project, not a production database.

Canonical site: https://mastidb.com
Source code: https://github.com/lokeshdevnani/mastidb (MIT licence)
Package: https://pypi.org/project/mastidb/ (`pip install mastidb`)
Author: Lokesh Devnani

## How it works

- Columnar storage: each column is stored as a 40-byte header (`.meta`) and a memory-mapped payload (`.mastidb`). Only the columns a query names are read.
- Dictionary encoding: values are stored once in a sorted dictionary and rows hold fixed-width integer IDs, so row i is found by arithmetic rather than an index walk.
- Roaring Bitmaps: each distinct value has a bitmap of matching rows, so a WHERE clause becomes a bitmap lookup instead of a row scan.
- Late materialisation: aggregation runs on integer IDs and strings are decoded only for the groups that survive.
- Independent segments: each segment answers a query on its own and returns a partial result that merges with the others.
- Hot loops are compiled with MyPyC.

## What works today

- SQL: SELECT, WHERE (equality, AND, OR), GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and COUNT, SUM, AVG.
- A command-line tool (`mastidb demo wikipedia`, `mastidb query`) and an embeddable Python API (`Table`, `QueryExecutor`).

## Known limitations

- Every column is stored as a string today; numeric types are on the roadmap.
- WHERE supports exact equality only: no ranges, inequalities or IN lists.
- Segments are scanned sequentially, not in parallel.
- COUNT(DISTINCT) across segments has a known correctness bug.
- Ingestion rewrites the whole directory; joins and subqueries are out of scope.
